subject.title: fix(gateway): regenerate native hook descriptors when relay unavailable after restart

question: When a Codex native PreToolUse relay cannot be reached, should OpenClaw fail closed or run a fully equivalent in-process policy path?
rationale: The current PR chooses fallback behavior at a command-authorization boundary, but its proposed path does not demonstrably preserve every native relay guard, so the permanent failure policy requires explicit ownership intent.

options.title: Require equivalent fallback
options.body: Permit recovery only for classified stale or missing relay transport errors after the fallback is shown to preserve loop detection, deferred approvals, rewrites, and deny behavior.

options.title: Retain fail-closed approvals
options.body: Land only the CLI gateway retry and continue denying app-server command approvals whenever native relay enforcement cannot complete.

options.title: Pause relay-policy changes
options.body: Hold this PR until the native relay failure taxonomy and canonical in-process policy owner are defined together.

recommendation.title: Require equivalent fallback
recommendation.body: Permit recovery only for classified stale or missing relay transport errors after the fallback is shown to preserve loop detection, deferred approvals, rewrites, and deny behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for both no-policy fallback semantics and deferred Codex approval behavior points to this owner.
